title: Anima vs. Docman: document management for GP practices
summary: Anima vs. Docman for NHS GP practices: compare document processing, AI summaries, SNOMED coding and clinical-system integration, with FAQs on switching.
body_markdown:
## What is clinical document management?


Clinical document management software helps GP practices turn incoming hospital letters, discharge summaries and other correspondence into an accurate patient record and a clear list of actions. The aim is to identify the patient, capture relevant clinical information, record appropriate codes and make sure follow-up work reaches the right person. Every stage matters, including the checks, approvals and follow-up that your team carries out.


Anima, Docman, BetterLetter and MyBotGP help GP teams process clinical correspondence. How much of each letter can they prepare, and what work is left for your team? Here’s how Anima and Docman compare.

## FAQs


### What should you check when comparing GP document processing software?


Take a representative set of clinical letters into each demonstration. Check patient matching, document summaries, SNOMED code suggestions, medication changes and follow-up tasks. Ask who reviews each output, how corrections are made and where the final document and codes appear in EMIS Web or SystmOne. Compare the time needed for exceptions as well as straightforward letters.


### Is Docman AI the same as Docman?


The product names describe different parts of the workflow. Standard document capture, filing and task routing should be assessed separately from AI summaries and coding assistance. Ask which modules your current contract includes and which functions require an additional purchase. This matters when comparing the cost of a Docman alternative.


## Are you planning a change in document management?


Before switching, agree how existing correspondence, outstanding tasks and historical documents will remain accessible. Include practice administrators and clinical coders in the evaluation. Define success using your own letter volumes, review time and backlog, rather than assuming that an advertised time saving applies to every practice.
